rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (kp 1.8, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1, narrow five-sensor array) is the best raced result at 366.7. On the oval, line_loss_events fell to 0.30 (from 0.85 at iteration 6), max_error to 0.044 (from 0.048), and completion rose to 18 of 20. The kp trend has been favourable at every step (2.5 to 2.0 to 1.8). The Evaluator's condition for keeping kp near 1.8 is met, so kp stays at 1.8. The s-bend (line loss 1.0, 0 of 20 finishes, progress 0.34) and the slalom (line loss 1.0, progress 0.17, all runs off track at the same point) are still the gap. Lower kd (iteration 7) and lower speed (iteration 5) both hurt, and wider sensor spacing (iteration 2) hurt. The one remaining lever that targets line retention at bends without changing the sensor layout or the control gains is the footprint size. I change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, one variable only. The 16 mm footprints at the existing 15 mm spacing overlap more and cover more of the tape. The outer sensors then see the line out to about x = ±0.038 m, up from ±0.036 m, so the robot keeps a reading a little further off-centre before the line is lost. Positions, sensor_weights, kp, kd, ki, base_speed and last_direction are unchanged. Expected result: oval results hold at or above iteration 8 (line loss about 0.3, max_error at or below 0.044), and s-bend and slalom line-loss events fall below 1.0 with more progress. Risk: the larger footprint blends the readings more, which could soften the signal on the tightest bends. If oval line loss or max_error rises, revert sensor_size to 0.012 and keep kp 1.8. Hypotheses: (a) s-bend and slalom failures are line loss at the bends, not a sensor-spacing gap; (b) a larger footprint reduces line loss without the gap problem that the wide array caused. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, compared against the iteration 8 baseline, plus noise_robustness.
